chunks: Al-Shaykh, may Allah Most High support him, informed me from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyād, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Shammūn, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from Mismaʿ Kirdīn, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:

“The man sentenced to stoning and the woman sentenced to stoning are to perform ghusl, be perfumed with ḥanūṭ, and wear the shroud before that; then they are stoned, and the funeral prayer is performed over them. And the one upon whom qiṣāṣ is carried out is in the same position as that: he performs ghusl, is perfumed with ḥanūṭ, wears the shroud, and the funeral prayer is performed over him.”

And Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā narrated this hadith from ʿAlī ibn al-Rayyān, from al-Ḥasan ibn Rāshid, from some of our companions, from Mismaʿ Kirdīn, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام: the like of it.

Al-Shaykh, may Allah Most High support him, said: If a dhimmī woman dies while pregnant by a Muslim, she is buried in the graveyards of the Muslims due to the sanctity of her child from the Muslim. Her back is placed toward the qiblah in the grave so that the face of the child may be toward the qiblah, since the fetus in its mother’s womb faces toward her back.

key_terms.الْمُقْتَصُّ مِنْهُ: the one upon whom legal retaliation is carried out
key_terms.ذِمِّيَّةٌ: a non-Muslim woman under Muslim covenantal protection
key_terms.يَتَحَنَّطَانِ: they are perfumed with burial camphor or funeral scenting

ai.seo_question: What are the burial and preparation rulings for a person to be stoned or executed in qiṣāṣ, and for a pregnant dhimmī woman carrying a Muslim child?
ai.summary: This report gives legal rulings concerning the preparation of those upon whom stoning or qiṣāṣ is to be carried out, stating that they are washed, perfumed, shrouded, and prayed over before or after execution as specified. It also includes a juristic ruling that a dhimmī woman pregnant by a Muslim is buried in the Muslim graveyard out of regard for the sanctity of the unborn Muslim child, with her placement oriented so the child faces the qiblah.
